answer: Persistent work escrow: each new agent identity must first complete paid, verifiable tasks whose escrowed rewards release only after a delay. An attacker cloning N identities pays N times the escrow float and N times the waiting-period cost, and abandoned clones forfeit their escrow to the atlas of active workers. Because rewards route through a shared ember pool keyed to completed task lineage, fake agents must also sustain real downstream work to keep their credit flowing. Every clone thus burns capital and time proportional to its count, like a river eroding extra channels.
